clue.text: Relative gets a quarter — that's a relief!

parts.note: NE, north-east, is one quarter of the compass
phew is the exclamation of relief

explanation.surface: Someone collects a quarter and sighs with relief.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's son is a family relation.

clue.text: Anonymous travelling salesmen

indicators.note: travelling suggests the letters of the word move around

explanation.surface: Unnamed travelling salesmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Unidentified, with no name attached.

clue.text: Fatherly friend swallows a tear

indicators.note: swallows means the word for a friend takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: a pal is a friend
a rent is a tear in cloth

explanation.surface: A kindly friend gulps back a tear.
explanation.definitionFit: Of or like a mother or father.

clue.text: Archbishop has vestment sent up

indicators.note: sent up in a down entry means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: a robe is a ceremonial garment

explanation.surface: An archbishop's robes are mocked.
explanation.walkthrough: The Archbishop of York signs himself with this Latin abbreviation of Eboracum, York.
explanation.definitionFit: The signature of the Archbishop of York, from the Latin name for the city.

clue.text: Leave by car to start a round

explanation.surface: Drive away, or tee off at the first hole.
explanation.walkthrough: In golf the first stroke of a hole is the drive, played off the tee.
explanation.definitionFit: To depart in a vehicle; in golf, to hit the opening tee shot of a round.

clue.text: Rent vehicle plant dormant for long period

parts.note: a rip is a tear
a van is a vehicle
winkle is short for periwinkle, the trailing evergreen vinca

explanation.surface: A hired van carries a plant that has lain idle for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like hire, but it is a tear.
explanation.definitionFit: Washington Irving's character slept twenty years, so the name stands for someone inactive a long time.

clue.text: Six points for a wine-producer

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
N and E are two compass points

explanation.surface: Six points awarded to a winemaker.
explanation.definitionFit: The grape-bearing climbing plant yields the fruit wine is made from.

clue.text: Key batsman?

explanation.surface: The most important batsman.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the openers are the two batsmen who start the innings.
explanation.definitionFit: A key opens a lock; in cricket, the first batter of an innings.

clue.text: Tie for which the football association need nets put up

parts.note: FA is the Football Association

indicators.note: put up in a down entry means the word is written upwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A drawn match where the FA needs to put up the goal nets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns NETS into STEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To tie is to secure or bind.

clue.text: Very light colour

explanation.surface: A very pale shade of colour.
explanation.walkthrough: A Very light is a coloured signal flare (named after its inventor Edward Very), so 'Very' is not 'extremely'; a maroon is a warning rocket.
explanation.definitionFit: A maroon is a distress rocket like a flare, and also a dark brownish-red hue.

clue.text: Painless treatment for dogs

indicators.note: treatment suggests the letters of the previous word are worked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: A vet offers painless care for pet dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: Springers and cockers are breeds of gun dog.

clue.text: Rosalyn and Ethel may be looking for happy relationships

indicators.note: may be suggests the names can be turned into something else by rearranging

explanation.surface: Two named women are seeking love.
explanation.walkthrough: The two names together hold exactly the twelve letters; 'and' is not fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Singles seeking partners, as in a personal-ads column.

clue.text: Business file

explanation.surface: A company's filing system.
explanation.definitionFit: One's trade is one's line of work; a file of people is a queue or row.

clue.text: Moslem leader said to be virtuous

indicators.note: said tells us the word for the leader is spoken and we write what it sounds like

parts.note: a mullah is a Muslim religious teacher

explanation.surface: A Muslim cleric is described as righteous.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent MULLAH and the target word sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethically upright and good in conduct.

clue.text: Measure encountered to the east

parts.note: met means encountered
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A measurement taken on meeting someone heading east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the east' puts E after MET, since in an across entry east lies to the right.
explanation.definitionFit: To mete out is to allot or deal out in portions.

clue.text: Fellow holds me up showing bad spirit

indicators.note: holds means the fellow's word contains the other piece

parts.note: a don is a college fellow

indicators.note: up in a down entry means the word reads upwards

explanation.surface: A college fellow lifts me, showing ill temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ME into EM before it goes inside DON.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiend or devil, an evil being.

clue.text: They secure the normal shipping rate

explanation.surface: Ropes hold firm at standard sea speeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Ties in rope hold things fast; nautical miles per hour measure a vessel's speed.

clue.text: Joined issue

parts.note: issue in the sense of offspring, born physically attached to each other

explanation.surface: Took up an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'join issue' is to start a dispute, but here 'issue' means children.
explanation.definitionFit: Conjoined twins are offspring born connected at the body.

clue.text: When cutting, it drives round the links

definitions.text: When cutting, it drives round the links

parts.words: When cutting, it drives round the links
parts.note: links read as chain links, not a golf course, driven round by a motor

explanation.surface: A golfer who drives round the course when slicing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drives', 'cutting' and 'links' suggest golf, but the links are those of a motorised cutting chain.
explanation.definitionFit: A power saw with teeth on an endless loop of links.

clue.text: Just a bit vulgar, perhaps?

explanation.surface: Only a little coarse, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: A vulgar fraction is one written as numerator over denominator, like 3/4.
explanation.definitionFit: A small part of a whole; in maths a vulgar one is a common ratio of two numbers.

clue.text: One guilty of a grave offence

definitions.text: One guilty of a grave offence

parts.words: One guilty of a grave offence
parts.note: grave read literally: a crime involving a burial plot, robbing corpses

explanation.surface: Someone convicted of a serious crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grave' looks like 'serious', but it is the tomb that is robbed.
explanation.definitionFit: Resurrection men dug up fresh corpses to sell for dissection, literally an offence at a grave.

clue.text: Foiled — the trespassers?

explanation.surface: Trespassers thwarted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foiled' means fought with a foil, the sword; fencing keeps trespassers out.
explanation.definitionFit: Fought with swords in sport; also enclosed, as trespassers are kept off by a barrier.

clue.text: Deserter held by soldiers without charge

indicators.note: held by means the deserter's word sits inside the soldiers' word

parts.note: GIs are American soldiers
a rat is one who deserts

explanation.surface: A deserter detained by soldiers is freed without charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without charge' looks legal, but means free of cost.
explanation.definitionFit: Free, costing nothing.

clue.text: Priest writes the final letter in time

indicators.note: in places the letter inside the word for a period

parts.note: an era is a period of time
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A clergyman pens his last letter in good time.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old Testament scribe of that name was a Jewish priest.

clue.text: Part of prison circle in large-scale fiddle

parts.note: a cell is one room of a prison
O is circle-shaped

explanation.surface: A prison wing caught up in a big fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: A big member of the violin family, fiddle being a nickname for a violin.

clue.text: An element of jazz in classical music

indicators.note: of says the answer is drawn out of the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A touch of jazz turns up in a classical piece.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'music' as the definition, but the answer is a metal, not music; 'An element' defines and 'of' introduces the hidden run in jazZ IN Classical.
explanation.definitionFit: A bluish-white metal, atomic number 30, used in galvanising.

clue.text: I rose to receive the king — a terrible person

indicators.note: to receive means the reversed piece takes a letter inside
rose in a down entry means the word reads upwards

parts.note: ego is Latin for I, the self
R abbreviates rex, king

explanation.surface: I stood up to welcome the monarch, a dreadful man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rose' turns EGO into OGE, which takes R inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A monster of fairy tales; figuratively a cruel, frightening person.

clue.text: Save up to get a brass instrument

indicators.note: up in a down entry means the word reads upwards

parts.note: save in the sense except means but

explanation.surface: Save up to buy a trumpet-like instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Save up' looks like putting money by; 'save' means except, and 'up' turns BUT into TUB.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest, lowest-pitched member of the horn family.

clue.text: Tom, for example, upset Roy in class

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

indicators.note: upset says the letters of the name are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: Tom upset Roy in the classroom, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns ROY into ORY.
explanation.definitionFit: A class is a group or division sharing a characteristic.

clue.text: Mix us lime for breakfast, perhaps

indicators.note: mix tells us to stir the letters of the following words together

explanation.surface: A cocktail instruction: mix lime for us at breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: A cereal of oats, nuts and dried fruit eaten in the morning, one example of a morning meal.

clue.text: Do without work in the pharmacy

explanation.surface: Go without a job at the chemist's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dispense with' means do without; a pharmacist dispenses medicines.
explanation.definitionFit: To forgo something (dispense with it), and to make up and hand out prescriptions.

clue.text: Capital naturalist

explanation.surface: A naturalist of first-rate quality.
explanation.walkthrough: Darwin is the capital of Australia's Northern Territory.
explanation.definitionFit: Australia's Northern Territory seat of government, and Charles, the evolution theorist.
